obligations.setup: Known stable binary input history following domain resets.
obligations.stimulus: Use known binary inputs stable around rising edges. Start from independently asserted and released core/falcon resets, and establish nonempty state only through accepted request/event history. Assert both resets at startup and while events are pending; independently reset the core and falcon domains at midstream with clocks running, observe asynchronous windows, then resume requests.
obligations.expected: Each reset clears only its stated domain immediately. Core response valid/data and logical pending state reset to zero. Falcon reset clears core_intr immediately while preserving core status for later propagation.
obligations.sampling: Compare native outputs after their corresponding rising edge or asynchronous reset assertion, after nonblocking assignments and combinational propagation have settled and before the next relevant input change or active edge. Correlate a response with the request accepted at the preceding core edge, and retain independent falcon-edge history. Any stated delay or scheduling mechanism that realizes this window is acceptable; no fixed nanosecond offset is required by the public contract. Observe asynchronous reset while asserted, including pulses between active edges.
obligations.checker: A self-contained native-port model predicts only from input request history, abstract mask/pending-event sets and independent clock histories. DUT and predicted outputs have separate wires. Compare all native outputs including held response data at the settled observation window defined above, including asynchronous reset observations. Report mismatches as UVM errors; finite stimulus, actual comparison/event counts and failure on missing intended windows reject vacuity. A fixed time delay is not required.

policy: Fixed obligation denominator. Distinguish missing coverage from local incorrect claims; preserve unaffected methods and semantic union. Sampling is judged by the public event/settled-value contract, not a hidden absolute delay. Preserve any real wrong-history, missing-window, or contradictory-expected-value error.
